text:
maria: Quick sync — proposal to stabilize a runtime metrics envelope + explicit cost-boundary mapping. TL;DR: go envelope-first to keep a single ingestion path for traces/metrics/logs, but we need a migration + cardinality mitigation plan.
sam: can you paste the rough shape of the envelope you have in mind?
maria: sure, very rough: ````json
{
  "envelope_version": "v1",
  "service": "payments",
  "host_id": "i-abc123",
  "billing_key": "acct_42",
  "payload": { /* trace/metric/log specific */ }
}
````
idea is top-level routing keys (service, billing_key, env) + small canonical header, payload opaque.
devon: my worry: queries that used to join trace->metric via trace_id will now have duplicates when both emit envelopes. how do we avoid double-charging and duplicated storage?
lekha: tradeoffs: envelope-first simplifies ingest but can increase cardinality if every log includes heavy tags. we should mandate a small canonical header (<=8 keys) and encourage payload pointers for bulk attributes. also strongly recommend `billing_key` as single string (no arrays).
sam: +1 on canonical header. also: need clear sampling semantics — sampled-trace vs unsampled-metrics. if we drop low-signal attrs at envelope boundary, how do enrichers rehydrate?
maria: plan for sampling/enrichment: 1) envelope contains `enrich_hint_id` (stable short id) 2) enrichment service can attach to that id post-ingest (late-bind) 3) we maintain a short TTL lookup (24h) for late enrichments. avoids bloating envelope.
lekha: that TTL lookup is acceptable but increases operational surface. can we instead include `billing_hint` (very small) that is enough for immediate cost attribution while enrichment fills the rest later?
devon: concern about backfills: dashboards that calculate cost per-deployment expect billing info at index time. We need deterministic fallback — if late enrichment misses, query should use `billing_hint`. agree on a single canonical field to prefer.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-ingest-feature-flag -> deploy at 2026-03-30 02:00 UTC (stub message).
natalie: from product/finance POV: we must measure cost delta in canary. request: expose a per-ingest token count + storage delta in Console during canary.
maria: ack — we'll add `debug.metrics.delta` and a lightweight dashboard. rollout proposal: feature-flagged ingest -> 2% production -> 10% -> 50% -> full. 2-week canary at each step with rollback on >10% cost regression or >1% error increase.
sam: query ergonomics note: add a mapping table so old queries (trace_id -> billing) still work without rewrite. minimal temporary compatibility layer = cheaper than migrating many dashboards.
lekha: ops followups: enforce envelope schema at gateway (reject if >8 header keys), add gzip preferred and warn on large payloads.
devon: retention note: 24h TTL lookup for enrich hints, but keep enriched canonical billing info in the envelope index for 90 days to satisfy chargeback queries.
maria: action items: open RFC follow-up with schema defs, migration checklist, cost experiments and the canary plan. I'll own the RFC.
natalie: approve with comments: run cost experiments on a representative tenant set (including big enterprise usage) and add budget alerts to rollout gates.
maria: thanks — I'll create the RFC + invite owners (sam, devon, lekha) to the doc and schedule a 30m follow-up next week.
ops-bot: incident-bot: reminder: there is a deploy freeze on 2026-03-29 00:00-06:00 UTC (automated).
